claims.text: Rapidly quenched FeCoNiTi has a dual-phase microstructure comprising fcc and hexagonal C14 Laves phases.
The FeCoNiTi system exhibits ferromagnetic ordering transitions near 1084 K, 214 K, and 168 K.
The C14 Laves phase is enriched in Ti relative to the fcc phase.
The fcc phase is enriched in Fe, Co, and Ni relative to the C14 phase.
The Ti-rich C14 phase acts as a magnetic sink for the fcc phase.
Ti-associated moments in the C14 phase couple antiferromagnetically to Fe, Co, and Ni moments in the fcc phase.
Antiferromagnetic coupling across the fcc/C14 interface reduces the net magnetic moment and saturation magnetization attributed to the fcc phase.
The C14 phase creates local strain fields at or near fcc/C14 interfaces.
The magnetically distinct C14 regions create magnetic-anisotropy barriers.
The fcc/C14 interfaces pin magnetic domain walls.
Domain-wall pinning and magnetic anisotropy from the C14 phase increase coercivity above the single-phase fcc limit.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys have coercivity capped at 100 Oe because their orbital moments are insufficient.
The dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy will exhibit a coercivity of approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
The dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy will have lower saturation magnetization than a Ti-free fcc reference.
Magnetic behavior in high-entropy alloys is sensitive to the compositions and morphologies of their constituent phases.
Antiferromagnetic Cr interactions can control or suppress the net magnetic moment in Cr-containing multicomponent alloys.
A C14-dominant alloy with similar Ti content and negligible fcc fraction can be compared with the dual-phase alloy to isolate phase-specific magnetic transitions.
Spin-polarized DFT on fcc configurations with and without Ti neighbors can test the spin-resolved density of states at the Fermi level and antiparallel local-moment alignment.
The hypothesis is falsified if the dual-phase alloy has coercivity below 200 Oe at 400 K.
The hypothesis is falsified if DFT finds neither a significant spin-DOS reduction nor antiparallel alignment associated with Ti.
